quotes: We report a case of congenital hypomyelination associated with cranial nerve dysfunction, respiratory failure, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy confounding the clinical picture.

Molecular genetic testing showed a complex de novo myelin protein zero (MPZ) mutation consisting of a 3bp deletion of CTA from nucleotide 550 to 552 and insertion of G at nucleotide 550 that by conceptual translation results in a frameshift mutation.

notes.statement: Smit et al. (2008) noted that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition with prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis, and areflexia. They added that most reported patients die within the first years of life, and that histopathology shows absent or thin myelin sheaths.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare condition characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia. Most of the few patients described in literature die within the first years of life.
Histopathologically there are no or thin myelin sheaths.

notes.statement: Kochanski et al. (2004) described congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy as a severe neuropathy with onset in early infancy, in which sural nerve biopsy showed nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and no myelin breakdown products.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy (CHN; MIM# 605253) is a severe neuropathy with early infancy onset inherited as an autosomal dominant or recessive trait.
Sural nerve biopsy shows a characteristic picture of nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products.

notes.statement: Szigeti et al. (2003) presented muscle biopsy findings in a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy due to an MPZ frameshift mutation that suggested an effect of abnormal innervation on early postnatal muscle fiber differentiation.
quotes: Muscle biopsy findings are presented that allude to the effect of abnormal innervation on early postnatal muscle differentiation.

notes.statement: Mandich et al. (1999) described congenital hypomyelination as a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy characterized by onset in early infancy, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities.
quotes: Congenital hypomyelination (CH) is a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities.

notes.statement: Mandich et al. (1999) found a de novo Q215X mutation in the MPZ gene in a patient with congenital hypomyelination. They concluded that this confirmed CH is allelic with disorders that have a less severe phenotype and a different clinical and neuropathological profile, such as CMT1B and Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.
quotes: confirms that CH is allelic with other disorders characterized by a less severe phenotype and a different clinical and neuropathological profile

notes.statement: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 novel mutations in the MPZ gene, which encodes the major structural protein of peripheral nerve myelin (P0), in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, or congenital hypomyelination. They suggested that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities but a spectrum of related 'myelinopathies' due to an underlying defect in myelination.
quotes: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.
This finding suggests that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities, but rather represent a spectrum of related "myelinopathies" due to an underlying defect in myelination.

notes.statement: Warner et al. (1996) hypothesized that the differences in clinical severity seen with MPZ mutations are related to the type of mutation and its effect on protein function, i.e., loss of function versus dominant negative.
quotes: we hypothesize the differences in clinical severity seen with mutations in MPZ are related to the type of mutation and its subsequent effect on protein function (i.e., loss of function versus dominant negative).
